f2.label: questions · q: You've established several educational institutions and ventured into healthcare
f2.value: You've established several educational institutions and ventured into healthcare and sports. What has kept you motivated throughout this journey?

f3.label: questions · a: For me, it has never been about how many institutions I could establish. It has
f3.value: For me, it has never been about how many institutions I could establish. It has always been about the difference they could make. Over the past three decades, I've been fortunate to work with people who share this vision. I've learned that you cannot build something meaningful alone. You need the right people, a shared purpose, and the patience to see your efforts grow. What keeps me going is knowing that there are still so many lives we can positively impact.

f4.label: questions · q: What do you think young Indians need today that perhaps wasn't as important a de
f4.value: What do you think young Indians need today that perhaps wasn't as important a decade ago?

f5.label: questions · a: I think today's young people have tremendous potential, but they are also naviga
f5.value: I think today's young people have tremendous potential, but they are also navigating a world that is changing faster than ever. A degree alone is no longer enough. They need practical skills, exposure to new technologies, good mentors, and the confidence to think independently. More importantly, I want young Indians to believe that they don't always have to wait for someone to offer them an opportunity. With the right knowledge and determination, they can create one themselves.

f6.label: questions · q: You've worked across education, healthcare, and sports. Why did you choose to ex
f6.value: You've worked across education, healthcare, and sports. Why did you choose to explore such different fields instead of focusing on just one?

f7.label: questions · a: I understand why people ask me this, but I've never looked at these fields as co
f7.value:
I understand why people ask me this, but I've never looked at these fields as completely separate. To me, they are all connected by one purpose: creating opportunities where they are needed most.

A young student needs access to quality education. A family needs dependable healthcare. A talented sportsperson needs a platform to prove their abilities. The challenges may be different, but the intention behind addressing them remains the same.

I've always believed that if you have the ability to make a difference in more than one area, you shouldn't limit yourself simply for the sake of staying in one field.

f8.label: questions · q: Do you think young Indians are too focused on government jobs and financial secu
f8.value: Do you think young Indians are too focused on government jobs and financial security rather than entrepreneurship?

f9.label: questions · a: I don't think there's anything wrong with wanting a secure future. Every young p
f9.value:
I don't think there's anything wrong with wanting a secure future. Every young person has different responsibilities, circumstances, and aspirations, and we must respect that.

However, I do believe we need to encourage more young Indians to look beyond conventional career paths. Entrepreneurship should not feel like an option reserved for people with financial backing or family businesses.

I want our education system to give students the confidence, practical knowledge, and support to explore their own ideas. A secure job is a respectable ambition, but so is creating something that might one day provide jobs to others.

f10.label: questions · q: What is one mistake you often see young people make when pursuing their ambition
f10.value: What is one mistake you often see young people make when pursuing their ambitions?

f11.label: questions · a: I think one of the biggest mistakes is expecting success too quickly. We live in
f11.value:
I think one of the biggest mistakes is expecting success too quickly. We live in a time when we see everyone's achievements, but rarely the years of effort behind them.

I often tell young people not to compare the beginning of their journey with someone else's years of experience. Everyone has a different starting point, and that's perfectly fine.

Focus on learning, improving your skills, and doing your work sincerely. There will be setbacks, and some plans may not work out. But I've learned that patience, consistency, and the willingness to keep learning can take you much further than the pressure to succeed overnight.

f15.value: I don't think of myself as someone who built one university. I think of myself as someone who has spent three decades trying to understand what India's education system actually needs - and then building institutions that try to meet that need, one at a time.

f17.label: Text: What began with the establishment of the Maharana Pratap Group of Institutions i
f17.value:
What began with the establishment of the Maharana Pratap Group of Institutions in 1996 has gradually grown into a network of educational institutions across different disciplines. Today, our institutions offer education in engineering, management, pharmacy, dental sciences, and other fields across Kanpur and Lucknow, with a shared commitment to quality education and practical learning.

This journey also includes five Pratap International Schools across Delhi and Kanpur. I have always believed that a strong educational foundation begins early, when children develop curiosity, confidence, and the values that shape their character.

f18.label: Text: In 2011, we established Pratap University in Jaipur, spread across a 100-acre ca
f18.value:
In 2011, we established Pratap University in Jaipur, spread across a 100-acre campus, with the vision of providing multidisciplinary education that prepares students for evolving industry needs and future opportunities.

Our efforts have also extended into healthcare through Maharana Pratap Hospital and Medicity. For me, education and healthcare have always been closely connected. Both play an important role in helping individuals and communities lead healthier, more independent, and fulfilling lives.

f25.label: Text: Over the years, my understanding of education has evolved, but one belief has re
f25.value:
Over the years, my understanding of education has evolved, but one belief has remained unchanged: a degree should open doors to opportunities, not mark the end of learning.

I have always wanted our institutions to prepare students for more than just examinations and employment. This is why I strongly believe in encouraging entrepreneurship and creating Startup Cells within educational institutions, where young people can explore ideas, develop practical skills, and gain the confidence to build something of their own.

f26.label: Text: I also believe that learning should not be limited to a single discipline. The c
f26.value:
I also believe that learning should not be limited to a single discipline. The challenges our young people will face in the coming decades will require knowledge from different fields, creative thinking, and the ability to adapt. Whether it is technology, management, science, or public policy, students should have the freedom to explore connections between subjects and develop a broader understanding of the world.

For me, the purpose of education is to nurture individuals who can think independently, take responsibility, and contribute meaningfully to society.

f28.label: Text: Having spent nearly three decades establishing and managing educational institut
f28.value:
Having spent nearly three decades establishing and managing educational institutions, I have come to understand that good intentions and well-designed policies do not always translate into meaningful results.

I have seen how challenges in implementation, limited resources, and changing regulations can affect institutions, educators, and students. These experiences have taught me that education reform must consider what actually happens inside classrooms and campuses.

f29.label: Text: My interest in the National Education Policy, vocational education, and improvin
f29.value:
My interest in the National Education Policy, vocational education, and improving access to quality learning comes from these experiences. I believe policies should be practical, inclusive, and responsive to the needs of students and educators.

For me, meaningful reform is not simply about introducing new guidelines. It is about ensuring that those changes create better learning environments, stronger institutions, and more opportunities for young people.

f31.label: Text: When I look back at the institutions we have established over the years, I don't
f31.value:
When I look back at the institutions we have established over the years, I don't measure their success only by the number of campuses, courses, or students enrolled. What matters most to me is how these institutions have influenced the lives of the people associated with them.

I have seen students from smaller cities gain the confidence to pursue careers they once considered beyond their reach. I have seen families place their trust in education as a way to create better opportunities for the next generation. And I have seen how access to learning can gradually change the aspirations of an entire community.

These experiences have strengthened my belief that education can create an impact far beyond the classroom.

For me, the true achievement of an institution lies not in how much it grows, but in how many lives it helps move forward.

f41.label: FAQs · question: Education system challenge
f41.value: What do you think is the biggest challenge facing India's education system today?

f42.label: FAQs · answer: Education system challenge
f42.value: In my experience, one of the biggest challenges is bridging the gap between classroom learning and the skills required in the real world. We have talented students and dedicated educators, but access to quality learning opportunities remains uneven. I believe we need stronger industry-academia partnerships, greater emphasis on practical training, and institutions that encourage curiosity rather than focusing entirely on examinations.

f43.label: FAQs · question: Success in education
f43.value: After establishing so many institutions, what does success in education mean to you personally?

f44.label: FAQs · answer: Success in education
f44.value: For me, success has never been about the number of institutions established or degrees awarded. It is about seeing students grow into confident, capable individuals who can make their own decisions and contribute to society. When a student from a smaller town finds an opportunity they once thought was beyond their reach, I feel our efforts have served their purpose. That is what continues to motivate me.

f45.label: FAQs · answer: How students learn and think
f45.value: I think the biggest change is that students today are far more aware of the opportunities available to them. They are curious, ambitious, and willing to explore unconventional careers. However, their expectations from education have also changed. They want practical knowledge, industry exposure, and skills they can actually use. I believe our institutions must recognise this shift and evolve to meet their aspirations.

f46.label: FAQs · answer: Is a degree enough?
f46.value: A degree is important, but I don't believe it guarantees success anymore. The world is changing rapidly, and employers increasingly value practical skills, adaptability, and problem-solving abilities. I always encourage students to look beyond textbooks, explore their interests, and gain real-world experience. Education should give young people the confidence to apply what they know, not just a qualification to display.

f47.label: FAQs · answer: Encouraging entrepreneurship
f47.value: I've always felt that students should have the freedom to explore their own ideas rather than see employment as their only option. Entrepreneurship teaches young people to identify problems, take initiative, and find solutions. That's why I support Startup Cells within institutions, where students can receive guidance and practical exposure. Even if they don't start a business, the ability to think independently will benefit them throughout their careers.

f15.label: Text: When I started my journey, I never imagined that one day I would be associated w
f15.value:
When I started my journey, I never imagined that one day I would be associated with so many educational institutions. All I knew was that there was a problem I wanted to address. I had seen bright, ambitious students in cities like Kanpur and Lucknow struggle to find the right educational opportunities. They had the talent and determination to succeed, but often lacked the resources and guidance to pursue their dreams.

That stayed with me.

f16.label: Text: When I founded the Maharana Pratap Group of Institutions in 1996, my goal was si
f16.value:
When I founded the Maharana Pratap Group of Institutions in 1996, my goal was simple: to make quality education more accessible to young people, regardless of where they came from. I strongly believed that a student's potential should never be limited by their hometown or circumstances.

Of course, turning that belief into reality required more than good intentions. It meant creating institutions with capable teachers, the right infrastructure, and an environment where students could learn, grow, and prepare for the future with confidence.

f17.label: Text: Looking back, I realise that I never approached this journey with a fixed roadma
f17.value: Looking back, I realise that I never approached this journey with a fixed roadmap of where I wanted to be thirty years later. I focused on what needed to be done at the time and tried to do it to the best of my ability. One step led to another, and each experience taught me something new.

f18.label: Text: What began with a desire to address an education gap gradually became a lifelong
f18.value: What began with a desire to address an education gap gradually became a lifelong commitment to creating opportunities. That belief continues to guide me in everything I do today.

f20.label: Text: For me, education has never been just a profession or a field of work. I have al
f20.value: For me, education has never been just a profession or a field of work. I have always seen it as one of the most meaningful ways to bring about change in society.

f21.label: Text: Over the past three decades, I have had the opportunity to establish schools, co
f21.value: Over the past three decades, I have had the opportunity to establish schools, colleges, and a university, each with its own journey and challenges. But through it all, one belief has remained constant: every child deserves the freedom and opportunity to discover their potential, regardless of their background, circumstances, or the expectations placed upon them.

f22.label: Text: I have always felt that education should do more than prepare students for exami
f22.value: I have always felt that education should do more than prepare students for examinations or help them secure jobs. It should encourage them to think independently, explore their interests, question what they don't understand, and develop the confidence to make their own decisions.

f23.label: Text: When our first school was inaugurated by former Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpa
f23.value:
When our first school was inaugurated by former Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee Ji in 1997, it marked the beginning of a journey that continues to shape my life today. What started with a commitment to making quality education accessible has gradually grown into a larger vision of preparing young people for the opportunities and responsibilities of a changing India.

I believe institutions must evolve with time, but the values they stand for should remain strong. Along with knowledge and skills, we must nurture integrity, compassion, curiosity, and a sense of responsibility towards society.

f24.label: Text: Even after all these years, I feel there is so much more to be done. And if my e
f24.value: Even after all these years, I feel there is so much more to be done. And if my efforts can help even a few more young people believe in themselves and pursue a future they once thought was beyond their reach, I would consider that a journey worth continuing.

f28.label: Text: The name Maharana Pratap has always held a special meaning for me. His courage,
f28.value: The name Maharana Pratap has always held a special meaning for me. His courage, self-respect, determination, and commitment to serving others are values I deeply admire. When I chose to name our institutions after him, it was more than a tribute. It was a responsibility to uphold those ideals through our work. Over the years, I have tried to ensure that every institution carrying his name reflects these values, not just in what we teach, but in how we educate, support, and prepare young people for life.

f30.label: Text: My journey has always been closely connected to where I come from. Growing up, I
f30.value:
My journey has always been closely connected to where I come from. Growing up, I saw how talented and hardworking young people in cities like Kanpur and Lucknow often struggled to find the opportunities they deserved. Many had the ambition to achieve something meaningful but lacked access to quality education and the right guidance.

Those experiences shaped my thinking and eventually inspired me to take my first steps into education. Even today, I believe that where a person comes from should never determine how far they can go.

f32.label: Text: Over the years, I have been fortunate to receive honours such as the Yuva Udyami
f32.value:
Over the years, I have been fortunate to receive honours such as the Yuva Udyami Puraskar, Jagran Ratna, and Yuva Sikshavid award. Each recognition has been encouraging, but I have never considered awards the true measure of my work.

For me, the greatest satisfaction comes from seeing students achieve their dreams, families find new opportunities, and institutions continue to make a difference in people's lives. These recognitions remind me of the responsibility that comes with my work and motivate me to keep contributing with the same dedication and purpose.

f46.value: Shailendra Bhadauria is an educationist, philanthropist and institution builder with nearly three decades of experience across education, healthcare and sport. He is a founding figure of the Maharana Pratap Group of Institutions (1996) and established Pratap University in Jaipur in 2011. His work spans nearly a dozen educational institutions, a 600-bed hospital, and Chetak Sports Private Limited, owner of the Dehradun Warriors. He has been recognised with the Yuva Udyami Puraskar, Jagran Ratna and Yuva Sikshavid awards for his contribution to education and social development.

f20.value:
I believe India's progress depends not only on the policies we introduce but also on how effectively they improve people's lives. Our schools, colleges, hospitals, and public institutions have an important role in turning national ambitions into meaningful change.

Having spent nearly three decades establishing and managing institutions, I've seen how policies translate into everyday realities, the challenges that arise during implementation, and the difference that thoughtful decisions can make.

Through this space, I want to share my experiences and perspectives on strengthening institutions, creating opportunities, and contributing to India's development in ways that make a real difference on the ground.

When I think about Viksit Bharat 2047, I see more than an ambitious national goal. I see an opportunity for every Indian to contribute towards building a stronger, more capable, and self-reliant nation.

I believe the young people studying in our classrooms today will play a defining role in shaping the India of 2047. That places an important responsibility on those of us working in education, healthcare, and other sectors to prepare them for the opportunities and challenges ahead.

f25.label: Text: For me, nation building is not limited to government policies or large-scale ini
f25.value:
For me, nation building is not limited to government policies or large-scale initiatives. It is also about the everyday decisions we make, the institutions we strengthen, and the opportunities we create for others.

The India we aspire to become in 2047 will depend on the work we are willing to do today.

f31.label: Text: I share my thoughts on India's development, the role of strong institutions, and
f31.value: I share my thoughts on India's development, the role of strong institutions, and how collective efforts can turn national ambitions into meaningful progress for every citizen.

f37.label: FAQs · question: Turning policy into results
f37.value: What is the biggest challenge in turning India's development policies into meaningful results?

f38.label: FAQs · answer: Turning policy into results
f38.value: In my experience, the biggest challenge often lies in implementation. A policy may have the right intention, but its success depends on resources, coordination, and the ability of institutions to deliver. I believe we need to pay greater attention to what happens on the ground, listen to the people affected, and remain willing to improve our approach when something isn't working.

f39.label: FAQs · question: Citizen contributions to nation building
f39.value: How can ordinary citizens contribute to nation building without holding positions of power or influence?

f40.label: FAQs · answer: Citizen contributions to nation building
f40.value: I've always believed that contributing to the nation doesn't require a particular position or title. A teacher who inspires students, an entrepreneur who creates jobs, or a young person who helps improve their community is already making a difference. I think nation-building becomes truly meaningful when we stop seeing it as someone else's responsibility and begin recognising the value of our own contributions.

f41.label: FAQs · answer: Nation building beyond policy
f41.value: For me, nation building begins with the work we do every day. It is about providing quality education, making healthcare accessible, creating employment opportunities, and strengthening communities. I believe governments can create the right policies, but institutions, businesses, and individuals must help turn those policies into reality. Every meaningful contribution, however small, plays a part in shaping a stronger India.

f42.label: FAQs · answer: Lessons from building institutions
f42.value: One thing I've learned is that progress takes more than good intentions. Even well-designed policies need strong institutions and committed people to make them work. I've seen how access to education and healthcare can change opportunities for entire communities. These experiences have strengthened my belief that India's development must be measured by the difference it makes in people's everyday lives.

f43.label: FAQs · answer: India's youth and Viksit Bharat
f43.value: I believe our young people should be active participants in shaping India's future, not simply beneficiaries of its progress. We need to encourage them to think independently, develop practical skills, explore entrepreneurship, and take responsibility for the communities around them. If we give young Indians the right opportunities and confidence today, they can become the innovators, leaders, and changemakers of tomorrow.

f10.label: Text: I have always believed that serving society is not limited to acts of charity. I
f10.value:
I have always believed that serving society is not limited to acts of charity. It is about understanding people's challenges and creating opportunities that can make a lasting difference in their lives.

Whether through education, scholarships, healthcare, or mentorship, my efforts have been guided by one simple belief: everyone deserves a fair opportunity to grow, regardless of their background or circumstances.

f11.label: Text: For me, Sewa is about turning this belief into meaningful action and encouraging
f11.value: For me, Sewa is about turning this belief into meaningful action and encouraging others to become part of that journey.

f13.value: I believe the true value of education becomes even greater when those who have benefited from it help others move forward.

f14.label: Text: The One Graduate, One Learner initiative reflects this thought by connecting gra
f14.value:
The One Graduate, One Learner initiative reflects this thought by connecting graduates from our institutions with first-generation learners who may need additional guidance and encouragement.

Through mentorship, academic support, and career guidance, the idea is to help young people navigate challenges with greater confidence.

f15.label: Text: The initiative has connected over 200 graduate mentors with first-generation lea
f15.value: The initiative has connected over 200 graduate mentors with first-generation learners across our institutions in Kanpur, Lucknow, and Jaipur. For me, what makes this effort meaningful is the opportunity to create a continuing cycle of learning, support, and giving back.

f17.label: Heading: Entrepreneurship Support Beyond the Classroom

f18.label: Text: I have always encouraged young people to think beyond conventional career paths
f18.value:
I have always encouraged young people to think beyond conventional career paths and explore the possibility of creating something of their own.

While scholarships can help students access education, aspiring entrepreneurs often need additional guidance and support to turn their ideas into reality.

f20.label: Text: Through Startup Cells in our institutions, we aim to encourage promising student
f20.value:
Through Startup Cells in our institutions, we aim to encourage promising student ventures by providing mentorship, opportunities to connect with experienced professionals, and access to limited seed funding for eligible ideas.

I believe even a small amount of support at the right time can give a young person the confidence to take their first step towards entrepreneurship.

f22.label: Text: For me, the purpose of any scholarship or support programme is to make a genuine
f22.value:
For me, the purpose of any scholarship or support programme is to make a genuine difference in someone's educational journey. Our scholarship initiatives are intended to help deserving students continue their education by supporting tuition fees and, where applicable, accommodation expenses.

I believe such efforts must be guided by transparency and accountability, ensuring that support reaches the students who need it most. More importantly, I hope these opportunities allow young people to focus on their education, develop their abilities, and work towards a future they can shape for themselves.

f7.label: Heading: Talent Doesn't Check Your Address

f8.label: SportCard: I got into sports for the same reason I got into education: because talent
f8.value: I got into sports for the same reason I got into education: because talent is everywhere, and opportunity isn't. Through Chetak Sports Private Limited, we own and operate the Dehradun Warriors in the Uttarakhand Premier League, but the bigger ambition is grassroots. I want to build structured pathways for cricketers who would otherwise never be seen, across as many BCCI-recognised state leagues as we can reach.

f10.label: SportCard: Pratap University's campus includes dedicated cricket nets, a multi-purpose
f10.value: Pratap University's campus includes dedicated cricket nets, a multi-purpose sports ground, and a fitness and conditioning centre available to all enrolled students, with priority access for those on athletic scholarships. Sports scholarships cover tuition fully or partially for students demonstrating state or national-level competitive achievement, renewed annually based on continued participation and academic standing - because the goal is athletes who graduate, not just athletes who play.

f12.label: SportCard: Indian education still largely treats sport as an extracurricular - somethi
f12.value: Indian education still largely treats sport as an extracurricular - something fit in around the real work of a classroom. I'd rather see it treated as a parallel discipline, with the same rigor and the same expectation of excellence. Programmes like Khelo India have done real work putting Indian athletes on a bigger stage; what I'd add is that the pipeline has to start on campuses, not just in dedicated sports academies. A university that treats sport as part of a student's education, not separate from it, is more likely to produce athletes who don't have to choose between a degree and a future in sport.

f14.label: SportCard: Uttarakhand doesn't have any of my education institutions, and that was par
f14.value: Uttarakhand doesn't have any of my education institutions, and that was part of the appeal, not a barrier to it - a genuine test of whether the instincts that worked in education would work somewhere entirely new. Cricket specifically, because it's the sport with the deepest talent pool in the country and the shallowest structured access outside the major cities. The Uttarakhand Premier League gave me a real, immediate platform to invest in that gap.

f16.label: SportCard: We're actively building the pipeline between our education institutions and
f16.value: We're actively building the pipeline between our education institutions and Chetak Sports the ambition is a student at Pratap University or one of our schools eventually training with or playing for the Dehradun Warriors. That pipeline is still young, and I'd rather be honest about that than overstate where it is today. What I can say is that it's a deliberate goal, not an afterthought.

f35.label: Text: Over the past three decades, my journey through education, entrepreneurship, hea
f35.value:
Over the past three decades, my journey through education, entrepreneurship, healthcare, and sports has shaped the way I think and approach challenges. I believe every experience brings a lesson worth sharing. Through this space, I hope to encourage meaningful conversations about leadership, opportunities, and India's future. I've learned that leadership is not about having all the answers. It is about listening to people, understanding different perspectives, and making decisions with responsibility.

For me, good leadership means building trust, encouraging new ideas, and creating an environment where people have the confidence to grow and contribute.

f12.label: caseStudies · title: Vocational Education & ITI Modernisation

f13.label: caseStudies · text: I have always believed that education must prepare young people for practical ch
f13.value:
I have always believed that education must prepare young people for practical challenges, not just examinations.

Uttar Pradesh's efforts to modernise Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs), introduce industry-relevant courses, and strengthen vocational training reflect an important shift towards skill-based education.

For students who want to enter the workforce early or pursue technical careers, these initiatives can open new opportunities. However, I believe their success will depend on the quality of training, industry partnerships, and the employment opportunities available after students complete their courses.

f14.label: caseStudies · title: ODOP & the Startup Story

f15.label: caseStudies · text: One of Uttar Pradesh's greatest strengths is the diversity of skills, crafts, an
f15.value:
One of Uttar Pradesh's greatest strengths is the diversity of skills, crafts, and industries found across its districts.

The One District One Product (ODOP) initiative has brought greater attention to local products and traditional industries, while the growing startup ecosystem is encouraging young entrepreneurs to explore new business opportunities.

I believe these efforts are particularly important for smaller cities, where talented individuals often have ideas and skills but limited access to mentorship, funding, and markets.

For me, real progress will come when more young people can turn their knowledge and ideas into sustainable businesses without feeling compelled to move to larger cities.

f17.label: caseStudies · text: I believe sports play an important role in developing confidence, discipline, te
f17.value:
I believe sports play an important role in developing confidence, discipline, teamwork, and leadership among young people.

Uttar Pradesh's growing investment in sports facilities, training centres, and competitive opportunities can help talented athletes pursue their ambitions with greater confidence.

My own involvement in sports has strengthened my understanding of how important structured opportunities are for young athletes. Talent exists in every part of our country, but talent alone is not enough. Young sportspersons need access to quality coaching, proper facilities, competitive exposure, and consistent encouragement.

I would like to see more young athletes from smaller towns receive the support they need to compete at higher levels.

f39.label: FAQs · question: ODOP and startup support
f39.value: How can initiatives like ODOP and startup support programmes benefit young entrepreneurs?

f40.label: FAQs · answer: ODOP and startup support
f40.value: I believe initiatives like ODOP demonstrate that economic opportunities do not have to be concentrated in major cities. Every district has its own strengths, skills, and entrepreneurial potential. With better market access, mentorship, technology, and financial support, young people can build businesses around local opportunities. I see tremendous value in encouraging entrepreneurship that creates employment while preserving and strengthening regional industries.

f41.label: FAQs · question: Sports and smaller districts
f41.value: What role can sports play in the development of smaller cities and districts?

f42.label: FAQs · answer: Sports and smaller districts
f42.value: I've always believed that sports can change a young person's outlook on life. Beyond physical fitness, they teach discipline, resilience, teamwork, and the importance of consistent effort. In smaller cities, access to proper training facilities and competitive platforms can make a significant difference. I would like to see talented young athletes receive opportunities based on their abilities rather than their geographical or financial circumstances.

f43.label: FAQs · answer: Uttar Pradesh's development journey
f43.value: Uttar Pradesh has been an important part of my personal and professional journey. Having established educational institutions here, I've witnessed how access to quality education and infrastructure can influence entire communities. What interests me most is how development is gradually reaching smaller cities and districts. I believe this shift can create meaningful opportunities for young people who previously had limited options close to home.

f44.label: FAQs · answer: Medical colleges and development
f44.value: I believe medical colleges serve two important purposes. They create opportunities for students to pursue medical education and help strengthen the healthcare ecosystem around them. When medical institutions expand into smaller districts, they can support local healthcare services, generate employment, and encourage professional development. However, I also believe infrastructure must be supported by qualified faculty, practical training, and adequate medical facilities.

f45.label: FAQs · answer: Vocational education
f45.value: Not every young person wants to follow the same academic or professional path, and I believe our education system should respect that. Vocational education provides opportunities to develop practical, industry-relevant skills and pursue meaningful careers. I would like to see stronger connections between training institutes and employers so that students can translate their learning into employment, entrepreneurship, or further professional growth.

f8.value: Every young Indian should leave education with at least one skill the market genuinely values - not as an afterthought, but as a core outcome.

f27.label: Text: Looking at how far India has come in the last few decades, I feel immense pride
f27.value: Looking at how far India has come in the last few decades, I feel immense pride and optimism about what lies ahead. Our progress in technology and digital infrastructure has shown that we have the ability to find solutions to challenges that once seemed impossible. The success of initiatives like UPI is a reminder that when we think differently and act with determination, we can create solutions that benefit millions.

f28.label: Text: I believe we need to bring that same ambition and confidence into our education
f28.value:
I believe we need to bring that same ambition and confidence into our education system. Rather than simply following models developed elsewhere, we have an opportunity to build institutions that respond to India's unique strengths, challenges, and aspirations. Our young people deserve an education that prepares them not just for the world as it exists today, but for the possibilities of tomorrow.

As India approaches 100 years of independence in 2047, I hope to see a generation that looks beyond traditional career paths and has the confidence to create opportunities for itself and others. I want our classrooms to encourage innovation, entrepreneurship, and independent thinking, where students are as excited about starting something of their own as they are about securing a good job.

f29.label: Text: For me, Viksit Bharat is not simply about economic growth or technological progr
f29.value: For me, Viksit Bharat is not simply about economic growth or technological progress. It is about building an India where every young person has the knowledge, confidence, and opportunity to contribute to the nation's future. And I believe education will play the most important role in making that vision a reality.

f41.label: FAQs · answer: Transforming education
f41.value: If I had to choose one, it would be transforming how we educate our young people. I want our classrooms to encourage curiosity, independent thinking, and practical learning rather than focusing only on marks and degrees. When students learn to solve problems, take initiative, and create opportunities, they become active contributors to the nation's progress. That, to me, is where meaningful change begins.

f42.label: FAQs · answer: Preparing for 2047
f42.value: I believe we have made considerable progress, but there is still a long way to go. Technology, industries, and career opportunities are evolving rapidly, and our institutions must keep pace. I would like to see greater emphasis on practical skills, industry exposure, research, and entrepreneurship. Education should prepare young people for challenges we may not even be able to predict today.

f43.label: FAQs · answer: Supporting young people
f43.value: I think we recognise the potential of our young population, but recognising it and nurturing it are two different things. Many talented young Indians still struggle with limited access to quality education, mentorship, and opportunities. I believe we need to create an environment where talent receives the right support, regardless of someone's background or hometown. Our young people deserve more than encouragement; they deserve genuine opportunities.

f44.label: FAQs · question: Entrepreneurship and India 2047
f44.value: Why do you place so much importance on entrepreneurship in your vision for India 2047?

f45.label: FAQs · answer: Entrepreneurship and India 2047
f45.value: I've always believed that a strong nation needs people who can create opportunities, not just seek them. Entrepreneurship encourages young people to think independently, identify problems, and develop solutions. But I also understand that starting something new comes with risks. That's why I want our educational institutions to provide mentorship, practical exposure, and the confidence to turn promising ideas into sustainable ventures.

f46.label: FAQs · question: A successful Viksit Bharat
f46.value: What kind of India would make you feel that the vision of Viksit Bharat 2047 has truly succeeded?

f47.label: FAQs · answer: A successful Viksit Bharat
f47.value: For me, success would mean an India where a child's future is not limited by their family's income or where they were born. I would like to see quality education, accessible healthcare, meaningful employment, and opportunities reaching every part of the country. If young Indians feel confident about their future and have the means to shape it, I would consider that real progress.

journey.title: The Beginning
journey.text: Founded the Maharana Pratap Group of Institutions with a simple conviction: that access to quality education should not be limited by geography or background. What began modestly has grown into a network of nearly a dozen institutions across Kanpur and Lucknow, spanning engineering, management, pharmacy and dental sciences.

journey.title: A Moment I Still Carry
journey.text: A year later, our first school was inaugurated by the late Shri Atal Bihari Vajpayee Ji a moment that shaped how seriously I took the responsibility of building institutions meant to last.

journey.title: Pratap University
journey.text: Established Pratap University in Jaipur, on a hundred-acre campus designed around a simple idea: a university should prepare students not just for jobs, but for a country changing faster than any curriculum can predict.
